How we selected the tissue

We chose the brain tissue with the most isoform-ratio QTLs (irQTLs: QTLs for an isoform’s share of its gene’s expression), since SCZ is a brain trait. The counts are Pantry’s conditionally independent cis-QTLs per GTEx v8 tissue (gtex.separate_kdp.qtls.tsv.gz, downloaded 2026-10-29).

  • Rank: among all 49 tissues, by the number of irQTLs. The table shows the top three tissues overall and every brain tissue.

Brain Cerebellum has the most among brain tissues: 6,755 irQTLs in 6,067 isoforms of 4,998 genes. Testis has the most overall. Pantry codes the two cerebellum tissues BRNCHA and BRNCHB. Its covariate files have 209 samples for BRNCHA and 175 for BRNCHB, the GTEx v8 sample sizes of Brain Cerebellum and Cerebellar Hemisphere, so BRNCHA is Brain Cerebellum.

How the runs were set up

  • GWAS: PGC schizophrenia, ieu-b-5102 (N = 127,906), z-scores harmonized to the UK Biobank (UKB) LD reference, as for the M-cTWAS paper.
  • eQTL and sQTL weights: the paper’s GTEx v8 PredictDB expression and splicing models for Brain Cerebellum.
  • irQTL weights (our definition): one trait per isoform, from Pantry’s independent cis-QTLs in Brain Cerebellum. They come from the genes significant in Pantry’s permutation test, q < 0.05.
    • Each isoform’s QTL is its strongest independent variant (smallest nominal p) among single-base variants in the UKB reference that are not strand-ambiguous.
    • The weight is that variant’s effect on the isoform ratio (tensorQTL’s slope); with one SNP per trait, only its sign matters.
    • Genes come from Pantry’s own annotation. We used top QTLs, not Munro’s prediction models.
  • isoQTL weights (added 2026-11-04; models from the paper, the top SNP is ours): one trait per isoform, from the isoTWAS prediction models of Bhattacharya et al. 2023 for GTEx v8 Brain Cerebellum (Zenodo 8047940).
    • The paper’s trait is one isoform’s expression (Salmon, GENCODE v38), predicted from SNPs within 1 Mb by multivariate models fitted over all of the gene’s isoforms. Only isoforms with cross-validated R2 ≥ 0.01 are released.
    • The models are dense (median 471 SNPs per isoform). We kept the SNP with the largest standardised weight per isoform (top 1), or the 5 SNPs with the largest (top 5, added 2026-11-04 at Xin’s suggestion), or the 3 largest (top 3, added 2026-11-05): see How the isoQTL SNP was chosen.
    • Genes are named from the paper’s PredictDB mapping (as for eQTLs), else from Pantry’s annotation.
  • Settings, as the paper’s runs: each QTL type is its own group, with protein-coding genes only and LD from the UKB reference. eQTL and sQTL weights are scaled (scale_predictdb_weights), and so are the top-3 and top-5 isoQTL weights, whose SNPs’ relative weights matter. The top-1 isoform weights (irQTL and isoQTL) are not scaled: with one SNP per trait only the sign matters. No thinning, one prior variance shared by all groups (shared_all), up to 5 signals per region (L = 5).
  • Nine runs: eQTL + sQTL (the paper’s QTL types), eQTL + sQTL + irQTL, irQTL only (added 2026-11-03, to test whether the irQTLs carry signal on their own), and eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL and isoQTL only, each with the top 1, top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform (added 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05). All use the same settings.
  • Not done yet: merging regions, checking LD mismatch, and merging duplicate isoQTL traits.

The top-5 weights pass the same steps and keep 353,412 isoform-SNP pairs for the same 76,213 protein-coding isoforms. cTWAS keeps 75,890 of them: cTWAS drops a weight’s SNPs that are not in the GWAS, and the trait survives while one of its 5 SNPs remains. How the isoQTL SNP was chosen

Each released isoTWAS file is one gene: one row per isoform and SNP, with the SNP’s model weight (Weight) and the isoform model’s cross-validated R2. We kept one SNP per isoform (our choice; 4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R):

  1. Keep isoforms with R2 ≥ 0.01 and SNPs with a non-zero weight (all released models pass).
  2. Keep the usable SNPs: single-base, autosomal, in the UKB b38 reference (same position, alleles in either orientation) and not strand-ambiguous (A/T, C/G).
  3. Standardise each weight: |weight| × the SNP’s genotype SD in the UKB reference. The isoTWAS weights are per copy of the counted allele (the models were trained on 0/1/2 genotypes, not standardised), so a rare SNP can have a large weight yet move the predicted expression little. The standardised weight measures how much the SNP moves the prediction across people.
  4. Keep the SNP with the largest standardised weight (ties: the smaller position). Its weight goes into cTWAS unchanged; with one SNP per trait only its sign matters.

This is the model’s most influential SNP, not a QTL lead variant: the released files have no association statistics.

Example: ARHGAP9’s isoform ENST00000393791, the trait behind ARHGAP9 in the joint run. It has 740 usable SNPs; these are the 10 with the largest standardised weight.

  • Rank: by standardised weight; Rank by |weight|: by the raw weight (tied weights share a rank).
  • Counted allele: the allele the weight is per copy of (the file’s REF column, which the isoTWAS training code counts). MAF and Genotype SD come from the UKB reference.
  • top_share (ours): the SNP’s standardised weight over the sum for all the isoform’s usable SNPs; Cumulative share adds them down the table.

The chosen SNP, rs324015, is only third by raw weight: rs3943363 has the largest weight but MAF 0.015. It carries 3.9% of the model, about as much as the next SNP (3.8%). Half of the model’s weight needs 68 SNPs, and 504 of the 740 SNPs carry less than 0.1% each.

  • kept_share (top 5) (ours): the summed standardised weight of the 5 SNPs kept per isoform, over the sum for all its usable SNPs.

Over all 76,307 isoforms the models fall into two kinds: small models (21,011 isoforms with at most 20 usable SNPs), where the chosen SNP carries a median 40.6% of the weight, and large models (37,156 isoforms with more than 500 usable SNPs, median 849), where it carries 0.8%. For the second kind one SNP is a poor summary of the model.

Top 5 (added 2026-11-04, Xin’s suggestion): the same steps, keeping the 5 SNPs with the largest standardised weight per isoform, each with its model weight (4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R with K = 5). The 9,938 isoforms with fewer than 5 usable SNPs keep all of them. The 5 SNPs carry a median 30.0% of the weight, against 7.7% for the top SNP, but only 3.4% in the large models.

What the tables and figures show

Parameters, the output of summarize_param():

  • group_size: molecular traits that reach cTWAS after matching to the GWAS and the LD reference.
  • group_prior: the estimated prior probability that a trait (or a SNP) is causal.
  • group_prior_var: the prior variance of a causal effect, shared by all groups (shared_all).
  • log_enrichment: the log of a group’s prior over the SNP prior, with its standard error; enrichment_pval is its p-value.
  • group_pve: the proportion of SCZ variance explained by the group; total_pve sums all groups and SNPs.
  • prop_heritability: a group’s group_pve over total_pve, the slices of the pie charts.

Convergence, from make_convergence_plots(): the estimates at each iteration of the parameter estimation (proportion causal π is group_prior, effect size σ2 is group_prior_var, enrichment is πG/πS, and PVE).

Gene-level PIPs: combined_pip combines all of a gene’s molecular traits and QTL types with combine_gene_pips() (by = "type", method = "combine_cs", filter_cs = FALSE). eQTL_pip, sQTL_pip, irQTL_pip and isoQTL_pip are the gene’s PIP from each QTL type; “–” means the gene has no trait of that type in a fine-mapped region. The mapping table assigns each trait to its gene: the paper’s PredictDB mapping for eQTL genes and sQTL introns, Pantry’s annotation for irQTL isoforms, and the PredictDB mapping (else Pantry’s) for isoQTL isoforms.

isoQTLs (2026-11-04): unlike the irQTLs, the isoQTLs stay enriched when eQTLs and sQTLs are in the same run.

  • log_enrichment is 1.86 alone and 1.48 with eQTLs and sQTLs (enrichment_pval 2.6e-17); the irQTLs fall from 3.36 alone to -1.62.
  • In the joint run the isoQTLs take 4.5% of total_pve, and all molecular traits together 14.7%, against 11.2% with eQTLs and sQTLs only.
  • Per trait the isoQTL signal is small: group_pve / group_size (ours) is 9.9e-08, against 9.3e-07 for eQTLs in the same run. The share is large because the group is large (71,057 traits).
  • These are the top-1 runs. With the top 3 / top 5 SNPs per isoform, the isoQTL log_enrichment is 2.77 / 2.94 alone and 2.77 / 2.94 jointly, and the isoQTLs take 15.7% / 18.3% of total_pve in the joint run. Much of this gain may be an artefact: see Top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform: checks.

Convergence

eQTL + sQTL converged in 17 iterations. eQTL + sQTL + irQTL stopped at 50 iterations without converging: the irQTL prior was still decreasing towards zero while the eQTL, sQTL and SNP estimates had settled, so its estimate is an upper bound. Both fine-mapped 204 regions. irQTL only converged in 20 iterations and fine-mapped 123 regions. eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1) converged in 17 iterations and fine-mapped 229 regions. isoQTL only (top 1) converged in 19 iterations and fine-mapped 193 regions. eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 3) converged in 19 iterations and fine-mapped 291 regions. isoQTL only (top 3) converged in 13 iterations and fine-mapped 265 regions. eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 5) converged in 19 iterations and fine-mapped 309 regions. isoQTL only (top 5) converged in 14 iterations and fine-mapped 287 regions.

Duplicate isoQTL traits

Caveat (ours): with one SNP per isoform, isoforms of the same gene often get the same top SNP. Their predicted expressions are then the same trait (up to sign), and cTWAS keeps them as separate traits. SuSiE splits a signal evenly over such copies and combined_pip adds them back, so a gene with many copies gets the prior of many traits.

  • Copies per gene and SNPs: how many of the run’s isoQTL traits have the same gene and the same SNP (top 1), or the same gene and SNPs with proportional weights (top 3, top 5); 1 = no duplicate.
  • susie_pip sum: the isoQTL traits’ susie_pip, summed over fine-mapped regions; Share of susie_pip is its share of the run’s isoQTL total.
  • isoQTL copies (gene tables below): the copies of the gene’s isoQTL trait with the largest susie_pip.

The copy groups take about the same share of susie_pip as of traits, so the duplicates do not drive the group estimates above. They matter for single genes. In the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1) run, PPIL2 (combined_pip 0.91) rests on 12 copies of its top trait, each with susie_pip 0.07, and TMEM25 (combined_pip 0.86) rests on 8 copies of its top trait, each with susie_pip 0.11. Their SNPs have GWAS |z| 4.74 and 4.68 (p 2.2e-06 and 2.8e-06), below genome-wide significance. ARHGAP9 rests on one isoform, ENST00000393791 (susie_pip 0.80, z = -6.4).

With the top 3 or top 5 SNPs duplicates are rarer: 86% and 86% of the isoQTL traits have no copy, against 65% with the top SNP.

Top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform: checks

Short answer (ours): with the top 5 SNPs per isoform the isoQTLs look much stronger, but several signs point to fine-mapping artefacts, not signal. The top 3 SNPs (added 2026-11-05) show the same signs, so the problem comes with any multi-SNP truncation of these models, not with 5 SNPs in particular. We have not tested the cause. Until we have, the top-1 runs are the safer result.

  • Top 3: in the joint run the isoQTLs take 15.7% of total_pve, and 86 genes reach combined_pip ≥ 0.8, 18 of them with |z| < 3. 6 of the 12 genes of the eQTL + sQTL run fall below 0.8. The gene list is not stable between top 3 and top 5: only 44 of the 86 genes at 0.8 with top 3 are at 0.8 with top 5 (CACNA1C: 0.01 with top 3, 1.00 with top 5). AMT, the example below, has combined_pip 1.00 with top 3: its two largest weights, the opposite-sign pair, are also the top 2 of 3.

Top 5 (2026-11-04):

  • In the joint run the isoQTLs take 18.3% of total_pve (top 1: 4.5%), and 105 genes reach combined_pip ≥ 0.8 (top 1: 15).
  • Some new genes have a strong marginal signal: CACNA1C (combined_pip 1.00, z = -5.2), CACNA1D (combined_pip 1.00, z = -6.9), MAD1L1 (combined_pip 1.00, z = 5.0).
  • But 4 of the 12 genes of the eQTL + sQTL run fall below 0.8 (combined_pip there, then with the top-5 isoQTLs): PTPA 0.92 to 0.31, ACE 0.91 to 0.51, TRPV4 0.89 to 0.00, GALNT2 0.85 to 0.62.

All columns are ours.

  • of which |z| < 3: genes whose top trait has a GWAS z-score below 3 in absolute value. A causal gene should show a marginal association.
  • Regions, traits take > 3 effects: regions where the molecular traits’ susie_pip sums to more than 3, so SuSiE puts more than 3 of its 5 effects on molecular traits. of which no SNP p < 5e-8: of those regions, the ones without a genome-wide significant SNP (largest SNP |z| < 5.45).

Open as PDF

Each point is one molecular trait (an eQTL gene, an sQTL intron or an isoform) in a fine-mapped region of the joint run (28,172 traits with the top SNP, 37,388 with the top 3, 40,263 with the top 5): its susie_pip against its own GWAS |z|. The dashed lines mark susie_pip 0.8 and |z| 3, and the shaded corner holds the suspect traits. With the top SNP, 0 of the 10 traits at susie_pip ≥ 0.8 have |z| < 3; with the top 3, 21 of 92 (21 isoQTL traits); with the top 5, 33 of 111 (33 isoQTL traits). With multiple SNPs, many isoQTL traits also sit at susie_pip 1 with only moderate |z|.

Example region 3_49279539_51797999 in the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 5) run. SuSiE puts 4.99 of its 5 effects on isoQTL traits and 0.01 on SNPs, although the strongest SNP (rs2624847) has z = -4.83.

AMT’s isoform ENST00000638092 gets susie_pip 1.00 with z = 0.10. Its SNPs:

SNP Region weight GWAS z r with rs3774745 r with rs11711407 r with rs4974078 r with rs12636232 r with rs11130237

rs11711407 3_49279539_51797999 1.359 0.86 0.84 1.00 0.00 0.25 0.25
rs4974078 3_47685722_49279539 -0.694 3.22 0.00 0.00 1.00 0.00 0.00
rs12636232 3_49279539_51797999 -0.050 3.66 -0.27 0.25 0.00 1.00 1.00
rs11130237 3_49279539_51797999 -0.050 3.69 -0.27 0.25 0.00 1.00 1.00
  • weight: the weight cTWAS used (the model weight scaled by scale_predictdb_weights).
  • r with …: LD between the trait’s SNPs (UKB reference), as cTWAS uses it. cTWAS sets it to 0 between SNPs in different regions.

The two largest weights, -1.39 on rs3774745 and 1.36 on rs11711407, have opposite signs on SNPs in LD (r = 0.84), so much of the trait is the difference between these two SNPs. Its z-score, which sums all 5 SNPs’ weighted z-scores, is near 0. Such pairs are more common among the suspect traits. In the joint run, 52% of the 33 isoQTL traits with susie_pip ≥ 0.8 and |z| < 3 have two SNPs with weights of opposite sign and |r| ≥ 0.8. The share is 39% for those with |z| ≥ 3 and 20% for the other fine-mapped isoQTL traits.

Our reading, not tested: keeping 5 SNPs of a dense model can keep such opposite-sign pairs. A trait like this can fit differences between the GWAS z-scores of SNPs in LD, for example where the UKB LD reference does not match the GWAS samples (LD mismatch). That would inflate both the isoQTL prior and the gene PIPs. Not done: cTWAS’s LD-mismatch check (diagnose_LD_mismatch_susie) in these regions.

  • eQTL_pip and the other PIP columns appear when a run has more than one QTL type.
  • Traits: the gene’s molecular traits in fine-mapped regions, over all QTL types.
  • Top trait: the trait with the largest susie_pip: its ID (an eQTL gene, an sQTL intron or an isoform), type, susie_pip and z-score (z).
  • isoQTL copies (isoQTL runs only): see Duplicate isoQTL traits.

All genes

Code: long_read_RNA/15.ctwas_gtex_isoform/:

  • 0.build_isoform_topqtl.R: the irQTL top-QTL weights and their mapping table.
  • 3.fetch_isotwas_models.sh: fetches the Brain Cerebellum isoTWAS models from Zenodo (only the byte range that holds them, on the login node).
  • 4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R: the isoQTL weights (top 1, or top K SNPs with a second argument) and their mapping table.
  • 1.run_ctwas.R and .sbatch: the nine runs (QTL types es, esi, i, est, t, esh, h, esf and f; h and f are the top-3 and top-5 isoQTL weights).
  • 2.summarize.R: this page’s tables and figures.
  • 5.top5_diagnostics.R: the checks of the top-3 and top-5 runs.

Downloads: tissue counts, parameters, gene PIPs, convergence, isoQTL steps, isoQTL copies and the top-5 checks (flags, example region, example trait, weight pairs, PIP vs |z| counts).
